title: A payer letter that writes the call's own name, member ID, claim number or date of birth with another script's look-alike letters or digits, with a digit for a letter or a letter for a digit (O/0, l/1, I/1, S/5, B/8, E/3), in pieces with a joiner between them, with a middle dot or a hyphenation point inside the name, glued inside a longer run of letters and digits, as a name part that is a month's word in a month-and-year phrase, or, in a held letter, the date of birth with a Roman month, the CJK date characters, its year in words, its month's word and day with no year, or run together as four to six digits at the start or end of a run
assertion: Each is the call's own placeholder, or the letter is refused. What ef3e8d20's reading refused stays refused whatever the look-alike reading finds beside the name (a number character glued to it, a look-alike digit after it in a held letter); a look-alike match is no item of a list and ends no label's window, so a number ef3e8d20 redacted after it stays redacted. An ordinary token is no form of a name of four letters or of a word and a number (`11am`, `CO13`, `JAN31`, `Week-5`), a short word of another script is no Latin name, a name stored in its own script is read as before, and the verb "may" after a number is no date of birth. The look-alike table's count and hash are pinned. Every row of rulings A' (406) and B (5) in `redact.residuals.json` is redacted or refused; the two name forms MOD-23 owns (a lower-case piece after a space or a period, letters spaced one by one) are pinned as they are sent today
noFileReason: Letters are written in memory by the tests, and the pinned rows are synthetic text in src/redact.residuals.json; no file.
